findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "verify_before_pay" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Should my agent pay this endpoint right now? Free key - a free pk_free_ key covers it against a shared 10 calls/day; $0.25 per call via x402 beyond it. Over MCP…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "verify_before_pay" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: verify_before_pay, get_liveness · Private data: verify_before_pay, get_circular_signal, get_token_metrics, get_provider_revenue · Public sink: verify_before_pay, get_market_summary, get_liveness, get_circular_signal, get_best_value_provider, get_changes, get_provider_revenue.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: verify_before_pay, get_liveness · Private data: verify_before_pay, get_circular_signal, get_token_metrics, get_provider_revenue · Public sink: verify_before_pay, get_market_summary, get_liveness, get_circular_signal, get_best_value_provider, get_changes, get_provider_revenue

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
